article_title: Pilot of a blended learning model on medical students' communication skills in the context of digital innovations.
citation: Töpfer J, Fritsch S, Wollny A, Romeike B, Endlicher D, Schrötter S, Schmitz S, Ciężka A. (2026). Pilot of a blended learning model on medical students’ communication skills in the context of digital innovations. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09662-1
title: H5P interactive online modules with immediate feedback for self-directed communication learning
description: H5P-based learning units delivered through the ILIAS learning management system provided interactive content including "quizzes, drag-and-drop tasks, and interactive videos". The modules "provided students with immediate feedback on the interactive learning content and supported the ongoing assessment of their own learning progress", enabling self-paced engagement before face-to-face consolidation sessions.
requirements: Learning management system (ILIAS) for content delivery
H5P authoring tool for interactive content
constraints: Empirical findings regarding performance improvements from H5P are inconsistent, though studies report high user satisfaction
examples: Module 1 covered narrative communication including active listening and consultation opening and closing; Module 3 covered genAI tools and communicating with informed patients
key_sources: Töpfer J, Fritsch S, Wollny A, Romeike B, Endlicher D, Schrötter S, Schmitz S, Ciężka A. (2026). Pilot of a blended learning model on medical students’ communication skills in the context of digital innovations. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09662-1

article_title: The effect of segmented-interactive video demonstration on student performance in procedural skills among healthcare students.
citation: Hamzah Nurul Rimadhayanti, Mohd Fadzil Abdul Hanid & Mohamad Ikram Zakaria (2026). The effect of segmented-interactive video demonstration on student performance in procedural skills among healthcare students. Advances in Health Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10459-025-10471-2
title: Segmented-interactive venipuncture video built in H5P with overlays, quizzes, and guided narration
description: A three-segment instructional video for venipuncture self-directed learning, developed with H5P and HTML5 so that it is platform-independent and integrates with a Learning Management System. It embeds overlay images, animations, formative quizzes, and prompts, applying "seven multimedia principles (e.g., segmentation, redundancy, signaling)" and Gagné's nine instructional events, with content such as needle insertion angle, bevel orientation, contraindication checks, and modelled patient communication.
requirements: Developed using H5P software with LMS integration for student access
Students completed three segments during self-directed learning within one week
constraints: Studied only for the venipuncture procedure in one undergraduate medical course
examples: Table 4 maps Gagné's instructional events to content such as "Image of the selection of vein" and "The bevel of needle position", each paired with a multimedia principle
key_sources: Hamzah Nurul Rimadhayanti, Mohd Fadzil Abdul Hanid & Mohamad Ikram Zakaria (2026). The effect of segmented-interactive video demonstration on student performance in procedural skills among healthcare students. Advances in Health Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10459-025-10471-2
